title: Proof starts with three products of our own
lede: Three products we built ourselves and one pilot at a gym. Each card says what it is and where it stands. Client work follows as it ships.

items.name: Bloop
items.kind: Own product · in build, piloting in Bologna
items.oneLiner: An AI concierge app that finds events and things to do in your city.
items.summary: Tell Bloop what you feel like doing, in plain language, and it proposes real events from a live catalogue, never invented ones. It is in build and piloting in Bologna.
items.tagline: An AI concierge app that finds events and things to do in your city.
items.built: A mobile app with a chat concierge and a feed of events across the city. You ask in plain language and it proposes real events from the live catalogue. Italian first, with English. A web admin for curating the catalogue.
items.proves: We can build an AI assistant your users talk to in plain language, and have it answer from your own live data.

items.name: Washiiba
items.kind: Own product · built end to end
items.oneLiner: A full marketplace platform with a customer app, a supplier portal and an admin back office.
items.summary: Washiiba is a laundry marketplace we built end to end as a complete platform. Customers order, choose a pickup window and follow the order live in a mobile app. Suppliers accept and handle orders in their own web portal. The operator manages orders, suppliers and users from an admin back office.
items.tagline: A full marketplace platform with a customer app, a supplier portal and an admin back office.
items.built: Three connected products. A customer mobile app for ordering, pickup windows and live order status. A supplier web portal where laundries accept incoming orders and move them through each step. An admin back office for managing orders, suppliers and users. Each order is offered to suppliers automatically, and the customer app runs in six languages. The first working version of all three was built in eight weeks.
items.proves: If your idea is a marketplace, we can build every side of it: the app your customers use, the portal your suppliers work in and the back office you run it from.

items.name: Kerf
items.kind: Own product · case study on public data
items.oneLiner: Finds where vegetation is too close to power lines, using free national LiDAR.
items.summary: Kerf turns free national LiDAR (IGN LiDAR HD in France) into a ranked list of overhead-line spans where vegetation is inside the clearance zone, measured in metres, then a work order for trimming crews. It is made for small electricity distributors and vegetation management contractors.
items.tagline: From free national LiDAR to a work order for trimming crews.
items.built: A LiDAR processing pipeline, a web map viewer with the ranked span list and per-span measurements, work order export (CSV) and a printable report. The case-study run covers 345 spans on 28.4 km of overhead line: 829.5 million LiDAR points, scanned in June 2021, processed in 83 seconds on one server.
items.proves: We can take raw public data to a ranked, measured result and a work order. Kerf is a case study on public data and is not yet validated in the field.

items.name: Recovery Room
items.kind: Pilot · live at a gym in Cagliari
items.oneLiner: Booking for a gym's massage chairs and pressotherapy.
items.summary: A gym in Cagliari needed a way for members to book its massage chairs and pressotherapy. We had a first version running the day we started. It now runs as a pilot on the gym's member list.
items.tagline: Booking for a gym's massage chairs and pressotherapy.
items.built: A booking page for phones, Italian first with English: pick a seat and a time, with no app and no password. A staff page with the day's schedule, no-show counts and the member list. Confirmation emails come from the gym's own address and bookings sync to its Google Calendar.
items.proves: We can get a small business a working tool in days, on its real member list.
